tagline: A global business and technology transformation partner, helping organizations to accelerate their dual transition to a digital and sustainable world, while creating tangible impact for enterprises and society.
hero_kpi_rationale: Capgemini positions generative AI and cloud as central drivers of client transformation, with systematic integration across its strategic offerings. This KPI captures real AI adoption in contracts, a key signal of leadership in technology services.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total value of sales realized by the company over the year.
kpis.description: Revenue reached €22.096 billion in 2024, growing 6.5% year-over-year.
kpis.signal: Solid organic growth in a demanding market.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.description: Operating margin stood at 13.3% in 2024, up 0.5 percentage points versus the prior year.
kpis.signal: Improvement in operating profitability despite sector headwinds.

kpis.name: Organic Free Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated from operations after investments and lease repayments.
kpis.description: Organic free cash flow reached €1.961 billion in 2024, up 8.2%.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.description: Capgemini had 340,000 employees in 2024, an increase of 18,000 versus 2023.
kpis.signal: Headcount growth aligned with client demand for digital transformation.

kpis.name: Women in Leadership Share
kpis.explanation: Percentage of women in management positions.
kpis.description: Women in leadership reached 35% in 2024, aligned with the group's 2030 target.
kpis.signal: Steady progress toward gender parity in leadership roles.

kpis.name: Average Client Satisfaction
kpis.explanation: Average rating assigned by clients on their contracts.
kpis.description: Average client satisfaction was 4.3/5 in 2024, measured against defined contractual expectations.
kpis.signal: High satisfaction level reflecting service quality.

kpis.name: Cloud Contracts Including AI
kpis.explanation: Percentage of new cloud contracts integrating generative AI capabilities.
kpis.description: In 2024, 40% of cloud deals included AI components, versus 30% in 2023, demonstrating rapid adoption.
kpis.signal: Sharp acceleration in AI integration across cloud offerings.

kpis.name: Training Hours per Employee
kpis.explanation: Average number of training hours completed by each employee.
kpis.description: Employees completed an average of 25.73 training hours in 2024, up steadily.
kpis.signal: Increased investment in digital and AI skills.

risks.title: Intense competition in IT services and digital transformation
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly mentioned in section 1.2.3 ('A demanding competitive environment'). Moderate language but central strategic positioning. Trend stable but structural. High weight: global IT services market highly fragmented with major players (Accenture, IBM, Deloitte).

risks.title: Dependence on strategic technology partners (AWS, Microsoft, Google)
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in section 1.2.4 ('Partners and ecosystem') and 2024 milestones (AWS, SAP, Microsoft, Mistral AI partnerships). Positive language but clear structural dependence. Trend up: proliferation of Gen AI partnerships. High weight: these ecosystems control key technologies.

risks.title: Talent risk and retention in AI growth context
risks.score_rationale: Implicit in section 1.1.2 (talent-centered values) and 2023 milestones (Data/AI team doubled to 60k in 3 years). Ambitious language revealing tension. Trend up: intensifying competition for AI/cloud talent. High weight: 340k employees, massive reskilling needs.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and protection of sensitive client data
risks.score_rationale: Cybersecurity mentioned as central pillar (section 1.1.4, 'at the heart of all our offerings'). Strong and repeated language. Trend up: rising threats, strict regulation (GDPR, NIS2). Critical weight: Capgemini manages sensitive data for Fortune 500 and government clients.

risks.title: Integration and performance of strategic acquisitions
risks.score_rationale: History of major acquisitions mentioned (Altran 2021, Leidos Cyber 2019, multiple in 2024: Unity, D+I, Lösch & Partner, Syniti). Neutral language but high integration complexity. Trend stable but recurring risk. Moderate-high weight: 4 acquisitions in 2024 alone.

risks.title: Sector regulation and compliance (GDPR, NIS2, regulated sectors)
risks.score_rationale: Implicit in section 1.1.2 (ethics, integrity) and 2003 Inland Revenue contract (regulated public sector). Moderate language but compliance omnipresent. Trend up: NIS2, GDPR, AI Act, critical sectors. High weight: government, finance, healthcare clients.

risks.title: Intellectual property and technology transfer
risks.score_rationale: Implicit in section 1.1.4 (proprietary solutions, 'proprietary company data') and deep tech acquisitions (Cambridge Consultants, Idean). Discrete language but strategic issue. Trend stable. Moderate weight: IP critical for differentiation but counterfeiting/copying risk.

risks.title: Geopolitical exposure and geographic footprint (50+ countries, India dependence)
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in section 1.1 (340k employees, 50+ countries, 12k in India by 2007, APAC expansion 2021-2024). Neutral language but massive exposure. Trend up: US-China tensions, Brexit, H1B visa restrictions. Moderate-high weight: delivery centers in sensitive zones.

ai_positioning.summary: Capgemini positions itself as a generative AI integrator within its transformation services, leveraging strategic partnerships and key sector offerings. AI is embedded in client processes and cloud offerings.
evidence: Capgemini cites 'market leading' capabilities in AI and generative AI (page 1)
AI is integrated in 40% of cloud contracts in 2024
The group is investing heavily in AI training for its 340,000 employees (25.73 hours per employee)
